title: Location Transparency Fallacy (Synchronous RPC)
pattern: Invocation of a remote service through a synchronous interface that lacks network-specific parameters (timeouts, fallbacks, retry policies) or separate error/success paths.
why_bad: Location transparency is a fallacy [32:276]. A local call takes nanoseconds and succeeds deterministically; a network request is unpredictable, has unbounded delays, and can block the calling thread indefinitely [23:170]. This reduces system capacity and causes cascading failures across services [34:264].
detection: Observing method calls on client wrappers or endpoint stubs where the invocation matches a remote network signature but lacks configured limits (timeouts, circuit breakers, asynchronous task spawning) [34:264].
fix: Enforce an explicit timeout and fallback strategy on all outbound network integration boundaries [34:271].
source: *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (Kleppmann), Chapter 4 & 8; *Release It!* (Nygard), Antipattern: Integration Points [34:264, 23:170].
